definitions.meaning: to stick loyally to someone, as in cleaving to a spouse
to split apart, the opposite sense of the same verb

explanation.definitionFit: This verb is a contronym: it means both to cling closely and to split apart.

parts.note: Che Guevara was the archetypal red revolutionary

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word turns it upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: white means pure, unblemished

explanation.surface: Raise the red flag, then raise the white one.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Lift' is the definition (to buoy someone's mood); the second, in a down entry, turns PURE upwards to ERUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift someone's spirits is to make them feel happier.

clue.text: Skim lure over bottom of filthy drain

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second
to skim is to take off the top layer, so the first letter goes

parts.note: to lure is to tempt

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down entry is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fisherman casts a lure over the bottom of a filthy drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skim' removes the top letter of TEMPT, leaving EMPT.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain a vessel is to take everything out of it, a verb synonym.

indicators.note: the spirit word takes the volcano in, enclosing it

parts.note: vim is energy or spirit
Etna is a volcano, whose head is hot

explanation.surface: A nation with spirit welcomes a hot-headed leader.
explanation.walkthrough: ETNA is the active volcano on Sicily, a fiery-topped 'hothead'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in South-East Asia.

indicators.note: the man comes after the slap, so the pronoun follows

parts.note: a slap is a swat
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone needs a bandage after a man slaps them.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind up in wrappings, as a bandage does a wound, is a synonym.

definitions.meaning: past tense of to worst, to defeat
a smooth woollen yarn and cloth

explanation.definitionFit: It is the past participle of a verb meaning defeat, and also a woollen fabric.

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written
incensed means angry, irate

explanation.surface: A country has made me flipping angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word intensifying 'incensed', but it reverses ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A state ruled by an emir, such as those of the Gulf, is a country.

parts.note: f is the musical abbreviation for forte, strong

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Ghana is a West African country

explanation.surface: A hound from a powerful country, without end.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a tall, long-haired hunting dog, a kind of hound.

clue.text: Wonder if poem matters, half left out

indicators.note: out signals the letters being knocked out of their order and rearranged
half of the word left means its first two of four letters

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a poem matters, with half of it left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes LE from 'left', and 'out' rearranges IFPOEMMATTERS plus LE into the temple's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple at Ephesus was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

indicators.note: about signals turning the word round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
yon is an old word for that, as in 'yon hill'

explanation.surface: A line is written about that particular author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ARC into CRA; 'written' only joins the pieces. 'that writer' wants to be a person, but the writer here is a drawing stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax stick used for drawing and colouring is a writing implement, so a writer in the object sense.

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre company turns to Hamlet, with an actor typecast in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a noun or 'turn to', but read as re-sort it shuffles TOHAMLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional printing cast metal type from molten lead, so this method literally is type cast.

parts.note: in cricket a paceman is a fast bowler

explanation.surface: A second fast bowler comes on, sending the ball like a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a paceman is a bowler who relies on speed rather than spin.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is carried into orbit by a rocket, hence the playful question mark.

definitions.meaning: numbers called out in descending order
a long-running British TV word and numbers quiz

explanation.walkthrough: The game show is a British daytime television quiz with letters and numbers rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures said in descending order before a launch, and also the title of a British TV quiz.

definitions.meaning: ran off quickly, made a dash
the term half-locked is written with a dash between its parts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolted' looks like 'locked', tempting a door reading; the second sense is the punctuation mark joining 'half' and 'locked'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to rush away, and to rush away is to make a dash.

definitions.meaning: trim as an adjective means neat and smart
a coniferous evergreen of the pine family

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective meaning neat and smart and the name of a conifer.

clue.text: Song for children in which parent attempts to cut through spiky plant

parts.note: pop is a familiar name for a father
goes are attempts, as in having goes

indicators.note: the cutting word goes through the plant, sitting inside it

parts.note: a teasel is a plant with prickly flower heads
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A children's song where a dad tries to hack through a prickly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parent' tempts MUM or DAD, but the father here is POP; 'in which' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known English nursery rhyme and singing game for children.

clue.text: Water, perhaps, that's in a kettle

definitions.meaning: water was one of the four classical ...
the heating coil inside an electric kettle

explanation.definitionFit: Water was a classical element, and the heating coil in a kettle has the same name.

indicators.note: in places the wickedness inside the attractive person

parts.note: dish is slang for an attractive person
evil is wicked inhumanity

explanation.surface: There is extreme cruelty hidden within a beautiful face.
explanation.walkthrough: DISH is informal for a good-looking person.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, fiendish describes something extreme, as in a fiendishly hard puzzle.

indicators.note: is is held inside the word for melancholy

parts.note: feeling down means feeling melancholy

explanation.surface: Feeling melancholy grips someone who has been rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to acknowledge someone as one's own is to reject them.

clue.text: Nothing special to find love in a toilet, when head over heels

indicators.note: the nil goes inside the upturned phrase
tumbling head over heels turns the phrase upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory
love is nil in a tennis score

explanation.surface: Finding love in a toilet is nothing special, falling head over heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head over heels' reverses the whole article-plus-toilet pair, not just one word; 'to find' and 'when' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and ordinary, from the default ice-cream flavour.

indicators.note: the woman's pronoun holds the magazine title inside it

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
Heat is a British celebrity magazine

explanation.surface: A woman holds a magazine's cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Heat is a UK weekly celebrity gossip magazine. 'cover' looks like a magazine's front page; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a blade in its scabbard is to cover it.

clue.text: Virgin son with a flat stomach?

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a flat belly has no pot, so it is pot-less

explanation.surface: A virginal young man boasts a flat stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsullied and pure, like a virgin page or record with no mark on it.

definitions.meaning: one who nicks, that is steals
British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a nicker is a pound, and to nick is to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: One who nicks things is a thief, and the same word is slang for one pound.

definitions.meaning: pull as influence, as in political pull

explanation.definitionFit: The word means influence or power and also a heavy hit.

clue.text: Break wind to woo lasses, then spread it about a bit

definitions.text: then spread it about a bit

indicators.note: break signals the letters being broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A crude lad passes wind trying to woo the girls, then puts himself about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break wind' is a phrase for farting, but 'Break' alone is the anagram signal working on WINDTOWOOLASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To have many casual affairs while young is an idiom about scattering seed widely.

indicators.note: the fool is punched into the word for utter, going inside it

parts.note: to utter is to say
nit is short for nitwit, a fool

explanation.surface: Reasoning with a fool, someone says the idiot was punched.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of a sound mind, the faculty one loses when going mad.

clue.text: Man getting Roosevelt sacked, partially recovered

indicators.note: re-covered read as covered going back, so the run is read in reverse
partially means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: A man brings down Roosevelt, who only partly recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards inside roosevELT SACked.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a piece is called a man, and the rook is also known by this name.
